# Research: Client Evaluations (MAG)

## Parser module design

**Context.** The MAG evaluation email body is semi-structured text generated by a billing system (`notasti@mag.com.br`) with fixed labels: `Competência:`, `Colaborador:`, `Fornecedor:`, `Avaliação Comportamental:`, `Avaliação Técnica:`, `Avaliação Prazos de entrega:`, and optionally `Feedback:`. The format is stable across the 4 real samples analyzed.

**Alternatives:**

- **LLM extraction** — tolerant to format drift; adds cost, latency, and an external service dependency. Overkill for a machine-generated fixed-format body.
- **Regex over labeled fields** — deterministic; fails explicitly when a label is absent or a value is invalid. Consistent with the requirement to never infer data.
- **Line-by-line state machine** — readable but more verbose than regex for extracting labeled values from a predictable layout.

**Decision:** Regex over labeled fields in a new `client_evaluation_engine.py` module — pure functions, no I/O, no FastAPI imports.

**Confirmation basis:** Confirmed without reservation in the reference spec: "Parser determinístico (regex sobre os labels fixos do corpo) — não é necessário LLM, dado que o formato é gerado por sistema e é estável. Extração fica como lógica pura (sem I/O), no mesmo espírito de `gabi_engine.py`."

**Consequences:** The parser is trivially unit-testable with raw string inputs. Any format change by the MAG system causes explicit `ValueError` (never silent wrong data), surfaced to the admin in the review screen.

## HTML stripping

**Context.** The n8n Outlook node returns `body.content` as HTML when retrieved via `Message: Get All`. The regex parser expects plain text. Stripping must happen in GABI, not in the n8n workflow, so the same parser handles both the manual (plain text paste) and automated (HTML from n8n) paths.

**Alternatives:**

- **`re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '', content)` + `html.unescape()`** — stdlib only; no new dependency; sufficient for well-structured Outlook-generated HTML.
- **`BeautifulSoup` (`beautifulsoup4`)** — more robust HTML parsing; adds a new pip dependency not currently in the project.
- **`lxml`** — fastest parser; also a new dependency.

**Decision:** `re.sub` + `html.unescape()` from the Python standard library.

**Confirmation basis:** Confirmed without reservation in the reference spec: "Uma abordagem lightweight de stripping (ex.: `html.parser` ou `re.sub` para remoção de tags) é suficiente; nenhuma biblioteca pesada de parsing HTML é necessária."

**Consequences:** No new pip dependency. Extra whitespace may remain after tag removal (e.g., from `<br>` elements) — acceptable because the regex parser matches labeled values ignoring surrounding whitespace. If Outlook changes its HTML structure to be more complex, this approach may need revisiting.

## `match_name()` adapter

**Context.** `gabi_engine.match_name(full, task_names)` normalizes each string in `task_names` via `norm()` (NFD + lowercase + strip combining marks), then splits by `"."` and checks `len(parts) == 2`. Team members are stored with `user_email` like `"pedro.santos@db1.com.br"`. Passing the full email directly would produce `["pedro", "santos@db1", "com", "br"]` after splitting — `len != 2`, no match.

**Alternatives:**

- **Duplicate `match_name()` with a different delimiter strategy** — avoids the cross-module call but duplicates 10 lines of normalization logic; risk of divergence over time.
- **Modify `match_name()` to accept email format** — changes a function used by all existing GA validation callers; violates the Open/Closed principle and risks regression.
- **Email prefix adapter** — extract the part before `@` from each `user_email` (e.g., `"pedro.santos@db1.com.br"` → `"pedro.santos"`). This is already in dot-notation first.last format and is compatible with `match_name()` unchanged.

**Decision:** Email prefix adapter in `client_evaluation_engine.py`. A helper `_email_to_prefix(email: str) -> str` returns `email.split("@")[0]`. The full list of team members is fetched once at ingest time; prefixes are extracted, passed to `match_name()`, and the returned prefix is reverse-mapped to the original `user_email`.

**Confirmation basis:** Analysis of `gabi_engine.match_name()` implementation (in use in the code). The `"first.last@db1.com.br"` email convention is project-wide (AGENTS.md: "`responsavel` derivation: email prefix uppercased and dot-preserved (`pedro.santos@db1.com.br` → `PEDRO.SANTOS`)" — confirms the prefix is exactly dot-notation first.last).

**Known edge cases:** Names where the email prefix is not in `"first.last"` format (e.g., a hyphenated name stored as `"josecarlos.silva"` vs. the email body writing "José Carlos da Silva") may fail to auto-match. The match then falls back to `match_status = "nao_vinculado"`, requiring manual admin resolution — acceptable given the mandatory review step.

**Consequences:** `match_name()` is reused without modification. No regression risk for existing GA validation callers.

## `_db()` extraction to `web/db.py`

**Context.** `_db()` is an SQLite context manager currently defined inline in `main.py`. The new `client_evaluation_repository.py` must import it to avoid putting SQL directly in the route handlers (per AGENTS.md: "no SQL queries in services — belongs in repositories"). Importing from `main.py` would create a circular dependency.

**Alternatives:**

- **Keep SQLite access inline in `main.py` for this domain** — consistent with all existing domains; defers the architectural improvement; deviates from `AGENTS.md`'s stated "repositories/ is the only contact point with external databases" principle.
- **Extract `_db()` to `web/db.py`** — enables the repository module; aligns with the principle; small, safe refactoring with zero logic change.

**Decision:** Extract `_db()` to `web/db.py`. `main.py` imports it with `from db import _db`. All existing behavior is preserved.

**Confirmation basis:** AGENTS.md: "repositories/: the only contact point with external databases (Oracle and SQLite)." The pre-existing inline SQLite pattern is acknowledged as a gap in adherence — this refactoring step closes it for the new domain without requiring a full migration of existing domains.

**Consequences:** One new file (`web/db.py`). One changed import line in `main.py`. Future domains can follow the repository pattern without the same workaround.

## API key authentication for the n8n integration endpoint

**Context.** `POST /api/integrations/mag-evaluation` is called by the n8n workflow — a machine-to-machine call with no browser session. The project's existing JWT session auth (OAuth2 Password Bearer) does not apply here. A lightweight auth mechanism is needed that n8n can configure as a credential.

**Alternatives:**

- **OAuth2 client credentials** — industry-standard M2M auth; adds significant complexity (token server, client registration) not justified for a single internal workflow.
- **Static API key via HTTP header** — simple, auditable, fits the project's security posture (internal corporate tool). Rotation requires a service restart but the rotation frequency for an internal workflow is low.
- **Shared secret in request body** — less conventional than a header; not directly mappable to n8n's "Header Auth" credential type.

**Decision:** Static `X-Api-Key` header validated against `MAG_EVAL_API_KEY` env var. New `_require_api_key(request: Request)` dependency in `main.py`.

**Confirmation basis:** Confirmed without reservation in the reference spec: "usar uma API key estática via header (ex.: `X-Api-Key`), validada contra variável de ambiente, no mesmo espírito de `SECRET_KEY`/`ADMIN_EMAIL` já usados no projeto."

**Consequences:** Simple to configure in n8n (Header Auth credential type). No token expiry to manage. Rotation documented as a known limitation: requires restarting the GABI service and updating the n8n Header Auth credential.

## Dashboard chart type

**Context.** The dashboard shows how evaluation scores evolve across competências for each professional. Three dimensions (comportamental, técnica, prazo) must be visualized on a common time axis.

**Alternatives:**

- **Line chart** — standard for time-series trends; visually communicates direction and slope; allows comparing three dimensions on one chart.
- **Bar chart** — easier for absolute value comparison per competência; less effective for showing trend direction.
- **Radar chart** — good for a single-point-in-time comparison of three dimensions; does not naturally represent time evolution.

**Decision:** `Line` chart from `react-chartjs-2`. Three datasets (comportamental, técnica, prazo) as separate lines. X-axis: competência labels in abbreviated format (`"jun/25"`). Y-axis: score 1–5.

**Confirmation basis:** Reference spec explicitly calls for "linha/tendência" (line/trend). `LineController` and `LineElement` are already registered in `PersonCard.tsx` — confirmed by code inspection; no new Chart.js registration required.

**Consequences:** Visual consistency with the existing chart patterns in GABI. The 1–5 integer scale on the y-axis means lines may be visually close together when scores are similar — acceptable for a trend visualization where the trend direction matters more than precise value comparison.
